aspects: Vaccines expose the body to an antigen without causing the actual disease
Innate immune cells detect the antigen and activate T and B cells
B cells make antibodies while T cells coordinate and kill infected cells
Memory B and T cells form, enabling faster stronger response on later exposure
Different vaccine types (live, inactivated, subunit, mRNA) present antigens to trigger this response
Boosters are needed because antibodies and memory wane or pathogens mutate to evade immunity

evaluation_claims.text: Pathogens such as viruses and bacteria carry unique molecular markers on their outer surfaces known as antigens.
An antigen is any structural feature that the immune system can identify as foreign.
Adaptive immunity is an arm of the immune system that mounts targeted responses against specific antigens and retains a long-lasting record of the encounter.

Vaccines can contain an inactivated virus, a weakened live strain, a purified protein subunit, or genetic instructions such as messenger RNA that prompt our own cells to temporarily produce the antigen.
Antigen-presenting cells such as dendritic cells engulf vaccine antigens and display fragments of them on their cell surfaces.
Dendritic cells migrate to the nearest lymph nodes, where they present antigens to T lymphocytes and B lymphocytes.
Activated helper T cells release chemical messengers that stimulate B cells.
B cells differentiate into short-lived plasma cells, which secrete large amounts of antibodies, and long-lived memory B cells.
Cytotoxic T cells are trained to identify and destroy host cells that become infected.
The primary immune response often takes one to two weeks to reach a peak concentration of circulating antibodies.
After vaccine components are cleared, antibody levels decline, while memory B and memory T cells can persist for months, years, or even decades.
A booster dose initiates a secondary immune response in which memory cells recognize the antigen almost immediately and proliferate rapidly into a large wave of plasma cells.

Through affinity maturation, dividing B cells accumulate small mutations in their antibody-binding regions, and cells producing antibodies with the tightest binding to the antigen are preferentially selected to survive.
Antibodies produced after a booster often bind to the target more effectively than those generated after the initial vaccine dose.
Circulating antibody levels naturally wane over time.
For pathogens that cause severe illness within hours or days of entry, having high levels of antibodies already circulating is vital to stop the pathogen before it establishes itself.
Memory cell populations can gradually decline over years, as is the case with tetanus.
Tetanus boosters are recommended roughly every ten years.
Pathogens replicate rapidly and can accumulate genetic mutations that alter their surface antigens.
When an antigen changes significantly, existing antibodies and memory cells may bind to it poorly or fail to recognize it.
The process of pathogen antigen change through accumulated mutations is known as antigenic drift.
The seasonal influenza vaccine and updated COVID-19 boosters must be reformulated regularly to match prevailing circulating strains.

reference_verifications.rationale: Evidence says antigens can be bacteria, viruses, or components derived from pathogens, but does not state they are unique molecular markers on outer surfaces.
Evidence defines an antigen as a substance that can trigger an immune response, not specifically a structural feature recognized as foreign.
Adaptive immunity uses antigen-specific receptors and generates immunological memory, remembering encounters for a lifetime in some cases.
Evidence supports dead/inactivated, live attenuated, and subunit-type vaccines (soluble subunit), but nothing on mRNA instructing cells to produce antigen.
Evidence says APCs such as DCs ingest antigens and present processed antigen with MHC on their surface, but not specifically engulfing vaccine antigens.
Evidence says DCs migrate to lymphoid organs such as lymph nodes or spleen and initiate T and B cell activation; 'nearest' and explicit presentation to both cells not stated.
Evidence says CD4 helper cells help B cells but does not mention release of chemical messengers/cytokines stimulating B cells.
B cells differentiate into plasma cells and memory B cells, with plasma cells producing antibodies; 'short-lived' and 'long-lived' and 'large amounts' not stated.
T cells attack infected cells and CD8 cells control intracellular pathogens; 'trained' and 'host cells destroyed' are not explicitly stated for cytotoxic T cells.
Evidence says clonal selection takes several days and viral clearance ~13.9 days in a model, but no statement of peak antibody concentration at one to two weeks.
Antibodies decline and memory B/T cells remain; memory cells persist for years. 'Months... decades' and 'after components are cleared' not directly stated.
Secondary response is quicker, larger, memory cells rapidly activate; but explicit 'almost immediately' and proliferation into plasma cells wave not stated.
No mention of affinity maturation, somatic mutations or selection.
Booster increases quality of antibodies and secondary response is more effective, but direct binding comparison is not stated.
Evidence states antibody levels naturally decrease/decline over time.
No evidence discusses pathogens causing severe illness within hours or days requiring pre-existing circulating antibodies.
Memory cell populations slowly decrease over years is supported, and tetanus needs boosters, but no evidence explicitly links tetanus to memory cell decline.
Tetanus boosters are recommended every ten years.
Evidence shows Omicron had many mutations in spike and replicated fast, but no general statement about pathogens rapidly replicating and accumulating mutations altering surface antigens.
Omicron mutations allow evasion of neutralizing antibodies and previously acquired immunity, supporting the idea for a specific case; memory cell recognition is less directly addressed.
No evidence mentions antigenic drift or defines antigen change through accumulated mutations.

Evidence says COVID-19 boosters may be updated for new variants, similar to strain-matched flu vaccines, and updated vaccines were recommended periodically. It does not state that they must be reformulated regularly; the UCLA text is tentative ('may').

quality.coverage_rationale: All six aspects are covered. Innate detection and vaccine-type differences are the thinnest.
quality.relevance_rationale: Nearly all content answers the question; the tennis analogy and the closing questions are brief and relevant.
quality.narration_rationale: The script has a clear opening and roadmap, defines its terms, and follows a logical order from primary response to booster to waning and mutation. It includes an analogy and a reflective ending. The tone is somewhat formal but easy to say aloud.

grounded_aspects.rationale: E-d14496f6da86 says vaccination mimics natural infection; E-8fbcb6c8a220 mentions active immunization by vaccine. 'Without causing disease' not explicit.

grounded_aspects.rationale: E-d14496f6da86 describes DCs/APCs activated, migrating to lymph nodes, initiating T and B cell activation; E-8fbcb6c8a220 covers innate then adaptive.

grounded_aspects.aspect: B cells make antibodies while T cells coordinate and kill infected cells
grounded_aspects.rationale: Only CTL cells and antibodies mentioned generally; helper T coordination and plasma cells not supported.

grounded_aspects.rationale: E-8fbcb6c8a220 describes memory cells rapidly activating on secondary infection; E-ccd3d559434f says memory B cells rebuild antibodies quickly after booster.

grounded_aspects.aspect: Different vaccine types (live, inactivated, subunit, mRNA) present antigens to trigger this response
grounded_aspects.rationale: E-d14496f6da86 covers live, inactivated, subunit, VLP influenza vaccines; mRNA not covered.

grounded_aspects.aspect: Boosters are needed because antibodies and memory wane or pathogens mutate to evade immunity
grounded_aspects.rationale: E-394facf40a0a (tetanus every ten years, antibody response), E-306db733a60b (protection decreases over time, variants, strain updates), E-ccd3d559434f (Omicron evasion).

additional_metric_details.notes: All scores are Claude judgments, not verified ground truth. Repair effectiveness compares coverage/narration, not factual truth. No revision or no retrieval is N/A rather than zero.

metric_semantics.reference_evidence_support_percent: Evidence entailment within the frozen reference corpus; not factual accuracy.
metric_semantics.query_coverage_percent: Coverage of a fixed six-aspect checklist derived once per question from the question text and shared by all systems; missing/duplicate judge outputs are normalized against that fixed denominator.
metric_semantics.narration_input: Coverage, relevance, narration and grounded-requirement judgements use the complete script with [E-...] evidence markers removed; claim extraction and citation metrics use the marked script. Aspect scores are continuous in [0, 1].
metric_semantics.narration_quality_percent: Ten-dimension spoken educational narration score; excludes factual truth.
metric_semantics.citation_precision: Share of emitted citation IDs that are identified as supporting the claim when verification is restricted to cited passages.
metric_semantics.citation_recall: Share of all citation-required extracted factual claims that have at least one cited passage judged to support the claim.
metric_semantics.evaluation_estimated_llm_cost_usd: Evaluator telemetry. CLI mode uses Claude Code's reported list-price equivalent; API mode uses the configured Anthropic per-token rates.
